5. Complete load transfer and recovery
Normal exchange
Phase	Physical operation	What carries the useful load
Initial inspection	Identify parts, inspect surfaces, observe wrench and pose, verify stocks	Original joint
Capture	Align pod centres, establish finite clearances, engage mechanical retention	Original joint, with catches available
Original release	Unwind preload and withdraw every cartridge/key/pin contact	Load transfers into the opposing shoes
Replacement installation	Insert inspected kit, engage positive retainers, observe depth and seating	Temporary cradle
Load return	Retract shoes in small bounded increments while observing pose and reactions	Increasing share on replacement
Isolation	Move each support clear; investigate any stalled or ambiguous operation	Replacement, with remaining catches available
Retrieval	Remove pods, tools, transport grips and cutting apparatus	Replacement
Final acceptance	Recheck intended wrench, pose, engagement, clearances and inventory	Replacement alone
Reset	Clean/inspect returned kits, replace consumed escape stock, quarantine faults	Replacement remains in service

The normal method does not command a calculated six-axis force split. That avoids creating a large hidden prestress from force-sensor bias.

A false seat is not accepted on a torque peak or seat switch. Positive retainer evidence and the subsequent actual load return must also agree. If the member follows an opening support beyond the bounded observation threshold, the controller stops and retains support.

Persistent or partly open isolation jam

After the replacement is positively retained:

Install the pod-owned head cage.
Confirm its ownership and the independent cutting route.
Cut the exposed member neck without reversing the jammed drive.
Retain the entire pre-cut energy stock until actual severance.
Withdraw the pod with the captured head.
Replace the damaged neck cartridge and service the failed pod at the rack.

The cut is not credited with a favorable force ramp. Its complete stored-energy release is charged to the primary joint and local capture apparatus.

Seized final support receiver

The order matters:

Establish that the member-side path is absent.
Mechanically grip the complete pod package.
Attempt normal foot-pin and receiver withdrawal.
If that remains seized, cut the independent foot neck.
Retrieve the pod.
Remove the grounded receiver/root
